source.title: Understanding MLP-Mixer as a wide and sparse MLP

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some numeric results appear only in figures, with no exact values stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: It tests the width-at-fixed-connectivity idea with Mixer, random-permuted Mixer, and sparse MLP models on image datasets, using different architectures and settings from the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own test-error and test-accuracy outcomes for width sweeps at fixed connection counts. Exact values from plot-only results are not reconstructed. CKA and singular-value results are not rows for the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures test performance while increasing effective width and sparsity at fixed connectivity. It never establishes that the compared networks have reached zero training error or that widening occurs beyond the width needed to fit. Thus it does not test V2's post-fit generalization claim. Its other results do not test the remaining versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: Mixers admit a wide, sparse MLP representation, and maximizing effective width and sparsity can improve performance at fixed connectivity. The authors also reproduce deterioration in extremely sparse SW-MLPs and connect it to trainability. They do not establish continued generalization improvement beyond a zero-training-error threshold.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Mixer and sparse-weight MLP architectures, with image-classification datasets and fixed-connection width sweeps; does not use the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setup or test interpolation-threshold double descent.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture (normal Mixer, RP Mixer, SW-MLP), effective width, S/C balance, and depth affect reported performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing effective width together with sparsity at approximately fixed connectivity generally improves Mixer and sparse-MLP test performance; sufficiently sparse SW-MLPs can plateau or deteriorate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed connectivity, jointly increasing effective width and sparsity can improve image-classification performance, subject to trainability constraints.

fits_no_version.finding: Normal and RP Mixers generally achieve their lowest error near C = S, which maximizes effective width and sparsity under the connectivity constraint.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Balancing token and channel dimensions can improve Mixer performance at fixed connectivity.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (paper text says preprint of a paper to appear in ICML 2024; provided venue is International Conference on Machine Learning).
record.problems: Several width-sweep values are presented only in figures and cannot be recovered exactly from the text. The paper reports results across different architectures and training recipes; the width trend is not uniform for very wide SW-MLP settings and the balanced S/C setting is identified as an optimum.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant rows omitted. CKA similarity, singular-value analyses, optimizer details, depth comparisons, and overfitting comparisons do not directly measure a listed version's specified behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance contrasted with natural-label training.
Whether test error keeps falling after networks reach the width needed for zero training error; convergence and the specified unregularized one-hidden-layer ReLU setting are not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under comparable tuning. Appendix D.7 changes learning rate along with optimizer and does not provide the required controlled comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its association with generalization gaps. Initialization singular values measure a different property.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 scope verdict for C = S is geometrically mistaken: C/S moves through a balance point while effective width first increases and then decreases. Section 5.3 also contains statements that error increases with width, conflicting with its opening sentence, Figure 5 caption, and conclusion; these appear to be wording errors. No exact plot values were inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train these architectures on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test performance.

Does not test the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, nor identify a zero-training-error interpolation threshold. Its width sweeps use Mixer, random-permuted Mixer, and sparse MLP architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, and ImageNet-1k.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks or isolate local connectivity as the cause of an advantage.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD for generalization.
Does not vary batch size to measure a large-batch generalization gap.
Does not test adding or removing dropout as a generalization intervention.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Normal Mixers
rows.operation_detail: Varied effective width by changing S and C while holding connection count fixed.
rows.value: Figure only; text says error was minimized around C = S.
rows.note: This sweep reports an optimum near balanced dimensions, rather than an unqualified decrease across all widths.
rows.check: C = S maximizes effective width at fixed connectivity. Minimum error there agrees with the width-improvement trend; it is not evidence of a reversal or an optimum at an intermediate effective width. Post-fit behavior remains unestablished. These are S-Mixers on the three smaller datasets and MLP-Mixers on ImageNet.

relation.reason: The paper discusses related generalization and architectural-bias findings, but its own experiments address width and sparsity without establishing V2's post-fit regime.

tranche.reason: The fixed-connectivity width and sparsity experiments do not establish zero training error or widening beyond the fitting threshold required by V2. No other claim version is directly tested or used as a tool.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated May 2024 and identifies the paper as forthcoming at ICML 2024. Section 5.3 contains contradictory statements about increasing error; its opening sentence, Figure 5 caption and conclusion report improvement with width.
